tools.name: ikas_get_app
tools.description: Confirm the connection: return the ikas Private App's id (the `me` query). A cheap way to check the store credentials work. ikas: POST /api/v1/admin/graphql { me { id } }.

tools.name: ikas_list_products
tools.description: List the store's products (name, type, total stock, brand, categories, tags and variants with SKU and barcodes). Filters are exact matches. ikas: listProduct.

tools.name: ikas_list_orders
tools.description: List orders with their package status, payment status, total, order date and customer id. Filters are exact matches. Orders contain customer data: read only what the request needs. ikas: listOrder.

tools.name: ikas_list_customers
tools.description: List the store's customers (name, email, phone). Use `search` for a free-text search, or exact filters. Customers hold personal data: read only what the request needs. ikas: listCustomer.

findings.detail: Description of "ikas_get_app" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ikas_get_app, ikas_list_customers · Private data: ikas_get_app · Public sink: ikas_get_app, ikas_list_customers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ikas_get_app, ikas_list_customers · Private data: ikas_get_app · Public sink: ikas_get_app, ikas_list_customers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
